subject.title: message tool: Feishu send action polluted by poll schema/guard prevents file send

question: Should the shared message tool solve this by action-scoping the LLM-facing schema, by sanitizing poll fields on `send`, or by keeping the current content-bearing poll rejection as the contract?
rationale: The remaining choice changes the public tool contract: stripping content-bearing fields can hide mistaken poll intent, while keeping the guard leaves schema-driven models able to block ordinary sends when the broad schema is exposed.

options.title: Action-scope the schema
options.body: Recommended: stop exposing poll creation fields in send-oriented schemas for non-poll actions/channels, while preserving strict poll validation for explicit `action="poll"`.

options.title: Sanitize send params
options.body: Strip poll fields from `action="send"` before the guard, accepting that a model's accidental real-looking poll payload will be treated as a plain send.

options.title: Keep current guard
options.body: Document the current behavior and require models/operators to disable or avoid poll-capable schemas when plain sends are critical.

recommendation.title: Action-scope the schema
recommendation.body: Recommended: stop exposing poll creation fields in send-oriented schemas for non-poll actions/channels, while preserving strict poll validation for explicit `action="poll"`.

likelyOwner.reason: The central choice is about the shared message tool's product/API shape, and this history trail starts with Peter's message-tool and action-handling commits.
